sentences.text:
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 56528 of 2022
Applicant :- Brahmanand Pal

Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Jagdish Prasad Patel,Lalit Kumar Tripathi
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.

Heard Sri Lalit Kumar Tripathi, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Ravi Kant Kushwaha,
learned AGA for the State-respondent.

The instant application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in Case Crime No.
0106 of 2018, under Sections 420, 467, 468 & 471 IPC, Police Station Ghiror, District Mainpuri,
during pendency of the trial in the court below.

FIR of the present case was lodged on 7.3.2018 against 32 persons including applicant and as per FIR, applicant being lekhpal of the locality on the basis of forged document, submitted a report in favour of some villagers and on that basis, their name were mutated over the State land.
Learned counsel for the applicant submits that entire allegation made against the applicant is totally false and at the time of date and alleged incident applicant was not working as a lekhpal but he was Registrar Kanoongo and therefore, entire allegation made against him, prima facie, appears to be totally false.

He further submitted that there was a procedure of mutation and merely on the basis of report of lekhpal, no mutation can be done and by the order of the Tehsildar mutation was done after proper inquiry and therefore, applicant cannot be held liable, if any, forged entry was made on Brahmanand Pal vs State Of U.P. on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/80534838/
1 the record.

entities.text: Brahmanand Pal vs State Of U.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He further submitted that applicant is a public servant and he is under suspension and he is in jail in the present case since 2.11.2022 and he is having no previous criminal history but after lodgement of the FIR of the present case, he was implicated in three other cases including one case of gangsters Act.

Per contra, learned AGA opposed the prayer for bail and submitted that there is specific allegation against the applicant that he was lekhpal and on the basis of forged documents, he alongwith other public servants entered the name of other co-accused persons on the revenue record and therefore,
it cannot be said that he is having no concerned with the alleged offence.

Learned AGA further submitted that the charge sheet in the present matter was submitted on 19.10.2018 and thereafter,
although applicant challenged the charge sheet before this Court in Crl. Misc. Bail Application u/s 482 Cr.P.C. No. 18471 of 2019 but his application was dismissed on merit and he was directed to appear within four weeks on 7.5.2019 but he did not comply the order passed by this Court dated 7.5.2019 and only appeared on 2.11.2022 i.e. after about more than 3 years from the date of order passed by this Court and this fact clearly suggested that applicant is an absconder and he is not co-operating with the trial and therefore, considering the allegation made against him and the fact that he is absconder, he is not entitled to be released on bail.
I have heard learned counsel for both the parties and perused the record of the case.

As per allegation applicant is lekhpal and he alongwith other public servants committed fraud and on the basis of forged document including the report a forged entry in public record was made and on the basis of the forged document forged mutation proceeding has been conducted and name of several co-accused persons have been recorded as the owner of the land in spite of the fact the land in question was State land, therefore, it appears that there are serious allegation against the applicant who was public servant, the lekhpal.

Further from the record, it reflects that although initially applicant approached this Court during investigation and his arrest was stayed and after investigation charge sheet was submitted then again, he approached this Court vide Crl. Misc. Application u/s 482 Cr.P.C. No. 18471 of 2019 but on 7.5.2019 this Court dismissed the application of applicant and directed him to appear before the Court concerned within four weeks but he flouted the order of this Court dated 7.5.2019 and did not appear within four weeks and appeared on 2.11.2022 i.e. after about more than one and a half years,
this fact suggest that applicant failed to honour the order dated 7.5.2019 of this Court and he is absconder, therefore, considering the allegation made against him and the fact that he is an absconder and failed to appear in spite of the order passed by this Court and he appeared after three and a half years, this Court is of the view that applicant is not entitled to be released on bail.
Accordingly, the instant bail application stands rejected.

Order Date :- 20.1.2023/Ankita  Brahmanand Pal vs State Of U.P. on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/80534838/
